title: (No AI) Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang
author: Lauren Feiner
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25824934/2192224191.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Nvidia's board is preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang following a [report from the _New York Times_ about a second alleged extramarital affair](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/technology/jensen-huang-nvidia-affair.html), just days after he admitted to a separate affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, [_The Wall Street Journal_ reports](https://www.wsj.com/business/nvidia-is-preparing-to-oust-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-30f421ad?st=yMDm9F). The second alleged affair was with an executive who reports to him, Nvidia's vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, according to the _Times_.

The Nvidia board will meet as soon as today to decide on Huang's future at the company, according to the _Journal_. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from _The Verge_.

title: (No AI) United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
author: Lauren Feiner
content:
![United Airlines](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/23176430/1237621702.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

United says it [won't let personal AI assistants book tickets](https://www.united.com/en/us/fly/help-center/digital-trust-center/artificial-intelligence/third-party-ai-agents.html) on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns.

The company says it hasn't yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book their flights, [_The Wall Street Journal_ reports](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/united-airlines-is-banning-ai-bots-from-booking-flights-5b514b38), in line with observations from other businesses like [Doordash](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/30/doordash-said-its-only-received-several-hundred-orders-from-ai-agents/). But United is concerned that agents could expose customers' information or make purchases they didn't intend, and potentially skirt federal rules about the kind of information airlines need to share with customers - like having them attest that their bags don't have explosives.

While agents can still show users United flights, they …
